The following trend was identified for MOV failure probabilities/rates for FTOC, FTOP, and SO events in the most recent 10-year period: • Decreasing trend in the low-demand MOV FTOC failure probability estimates, which is highly statistically significant with a p-value of 0.005 (see Figure 1). The same trend was observed in the 2022, 2020, 2018, and 2016 MOV update studies [2], [9]–[11] as extremely statistically significant, highly statistically significant, or statistically significant. • Decreasing trend in the high-demand MOV SO failure rate estimates, which is statistically significant with a p-value of 0.041 (see Figure 6). This is a new trend that was not observed in previous MOV update studies. 18 Figure 1. Failure probability estimate trend for low-demand MOV FTOC. Figure 2. ENGINEERING ANALYSIS 4.1 Engineering Trends This section presents frequency trends for MOV demands and failure events. The data are normalized by reactor year for plants that report data for the equipment being trended. The trends provide an overview of the demand counts and failure counts associated with each failure mode across the years. Figure 7 to Figure 14 provide the plots for frequency of MOV demands, FTOC events, FTOP events, and SO events: • Figure 7 and Figure 8 show the trends in frequency of FTOC demands (demands per reactor year) for low-demand and high-demand MOVs, respectively • Figure 9 and Figure 10 show the trends in frequency of FTOC events (events per reactor year) for low-demand and high-demand MOVs, respectively • Figure 11 and Figure 12 show the trends in frequency of FTOP events (events per reactor year) for low-demand and high-demand MOVs, respectively • Figure 13 and Figure 14 show the trends in frequency of SO events (events per reactor year) for low- demand and high-demand MOVs, respectively. The data for the figures listed above are provided in Section 6. The systems from Table 1 are trended together for each figure. The rate methods described in Section 2 of Overview and Reference [3] are used.
